rules.sentence: Appendectomy is indicated in patients with a history, physical examination, and laboratory and imaging findings consistent with acute uncomplicated appendicitis.
Uncomplicated or simple appendicitis is defined as an inflamed appendix without evidence of necrosis or perforation.[2]
The efficacy of antibiotics as the primary treatment for acute uncomplicated appendicitis has been extensively researched, yielding mixed and contradictory results and conclusions.[12][13][14]
Adverse events, including the incidence of 30-day postintervention peritonitis, were higher in the antibiotic therapy arm of one trial.
However, other trials support the feasibility of antibiotic therapy alone despite the cumulative incidence of appendicitis recurrence for uncomplicated acute appendicitis.[15]
